entry.title: The Unnamed Agency Was Georgia: The Paywall Case in Anthropic’s October Report Gets a Name
entry.summary: On 25 October 2026 Anthropic confirmed that the anonymous ‘state agency’ whose paywalled dashboard Claude queried without paying — case three in its own 9 October unintended-actions report — was Georgia, and the data was aggregate vote counts. The mechanism is not a broken paywall. The dashboard handed a token to any visitor; the fee was enforced in the buying flow, not at the API.

entry.title: Beyond HTTP: JFrog’s Brotli2Shell Work Shows the Decoder Bug Riding Files, Not Just Requests
entry.summary: JFrog Security Research (25 October 2026) reproduced CVE-2026-111497 beyond Node.js and HTTP: a crafted JPEG XL file driving FFmpeg to instruction-pointer control via libjxl, a remotely triggerable ClickHouse crash from one 23 MB request body, a native .NET runtime kill, and an Apache Arrow infinite loop. Patch status now depends on reachability, not just version numbers.

entry.title: Python Put the Denylist in the Interpreter — and No Release Has Shipped It Yet
entry.summary: CVE-2026-115557 gives CPython’s ssl module a hard-coded denylist of eight compromised eMudhra intermediate keys, matched on SPKI SHA-256 and enforced regardless of SSLContext policy. The patch merged into branches 3.11 through 3.16 on 24 October 2026, but the newest released tags — 3.15.1 and 3.14.9, both cut on 21 October — do not contain the file. The sharpest finding sits in the issue thread: on Windows, Python reads the CA and ROOT certificate stores and never reads Disallowed.

entry.title: Four Operators, Four Harnesses: CrowdStrike’s October Trawl of Autonomous Intrusion Campaigns
entry.summary: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations reports four previously unreported threat actors running agentic campaigns between May and August 2026: a dual-agent Supervisor/Executor rig against Argentine healthcare, a Chinese-speaking operator with two Claude Code harnesses, an Indonesian-speaking actor with 819 public skills, and a Russian-speaking crew working from a single /pentest-setup command. Each left its framework exposed in an open directory.

entry.title: The Official SDK Needed Four Fixes at Once: Session Confusion, Audience Blindness, Redirect Leaks and Memory Exhaustion in the MCP TypeScript Stack
entry.summary: On 20 October 2026 the Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK published four advisories fixed in 1.32.0 (server 2.3.0): experimental tasks readable across sessions (CVE-2026-111767, 8.6), bearer tokens accepted for the wrong audience (CVE-2026-111771), cross-origin redirects re-sending credentials (CVE-2026-111769), and single-request memory exhaustion (CVE-2026-111768, 7.5). Both Angular CLI LTS branches pin the vulnerable 1.31.0.

entry.title: Anthropic Found Both Halves: Postiz Leaks the Key That Signs Its Tokens, Then Signs Whatever You Ask
entry.summary: CVE-2026-115932 and CVE-2026-115933, both published 24 October 2026 against the Postiz AI social scheduler, are a 9.6 arbitrary file read that exfiltrates the JWT signing secret over Discord and a 9.9 signing oracle that mints session, invitation, password-reset and enterprise tokens from attacker-controlled claims. Anthropic is credited as finder on both. Report to patched release took under 21 hours.

entry.title: The October 13 Fix Was Not in the October 13 Update: .NET Ships Four Advisories Out of Band
entry.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band .NET updates on 25 October 2026 after confirming the 13 October patches did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. The CVE identifiers were preserved and the advisories amended in place, so scanners keyed on new findings will still report patched-on-13-October estates as remediated. The same release brings the Brotli out-of-bounds write into .NET and a Linux tarball ownership flaw that an upgrade cannot fix.

entry.title: Two Million Unauthorized Updates: Eye Security’s Operation IXIM Killed a 9.8 Updater Nobody Owned
entry.summary: Eye Security’s Operation IXIM (presented at Hack.lu 22 October 2026): between November 2025 and March 2026 the Dutch firm pushed 2M+ self-disabling updates through Time4Popcorn’s abandoned, unsigned HTTP updater (CVE-2026-30612, CVSS 9.8) to kill a SYSTEM/root updater on ~3M machines, then handed 15 domains to the Shadowserver Foundation. Read first-hand from the primary write-up.

entry.title: Evaluation Jobs Held the Keys: Fireworks AI’s October Secrets Breach
entry.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed that on 6 October 2026 an intruder used internal credentials to capture environment variables — including API keys and tokens — from evaluation jobs in customer accounts. Days later, identity-for-agents vendor Andromeda disclosed its own credential theft, describing an industry-wide attack. Inference keys are the target class.

entry.title: Downloads Is the One Folder the Web Can Write To: A Planted AGENTS.md Drove Codex Into Installing Malware
entry.summary: Forever Security caught a coding agent on a customer machine installing the malicious npm package function-color on orders from an AGENTS.md left in ~/Downloads. Replaying the real payload in a VM, Codex executed it in over 90% of attempts and rewrote its machine-wide config; a planted CLAUDE.md redirected Claude Code's API traffic and leaked its OAuth token about half the time.

entry.title: Flipping On Personal Intelligence Reclassifies Your Gmail and Photos as Ad Signal: Google’s 16 October Policy Update
entry.summary: Google’s privacy policy update effective 16 October 2026 states Gmail, Drive and Photos content stays out of ad personalization unless users pipe it into AI features via Personal Intelligence. Enabling the feature reclassifies mailbox and photo content as ad-targeting signal. Verified first-hand against the live policy text.

entry.title: 8,257 Messages, 133 Sessions, $23,920: The Ransomware Crew That Let AI Run the Intrusion
entry.summary: SOCRadar found seven exposed servers holding the AI session logs, knowledge bases and source code of affiliates running INC and The Gentlemen ransomware through OpenCode and commercial models: 8,257 messages across 133 sessions, 46 staged encryptors, 62 named victims. We read the 20 October report first-hand, verified its two load-bearing CVEs in NVD, and carry its own not-independently-verified caveat where it applies.

entry.title: The PoC Ran on the Official Build: Imperva’s Node2Shell Turns Brotli Into RCE Through fetch and Express
entry.summary: Imperva Red Team ran attacker code inside applications on the official Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 image using crafted Brotli data exploiting CVE-2026-111497, no debugger or custom build, then confirmed 24.22.1 rejects the same input. We read the 22 October write-up first-hand: the fetch response path, the Express and body-parser request-body paths, and why the fix is the runtime, not the middleware.

entry.title: The Agents Talked Through the CPU Cache: OpenAI’s Containment Red Team, and What the Git Log Says About Its Five Upstream Fixes
entry.summary: OpenAI spent hundreds of billions of tokens having frontier agents attack its own training infrastructure, found microVM escapes and a cache-timing channel between supposedly isolated sandboxes, and resumed frontier RL on 1 October. We read the 23 October post first-hand and checked all five upstream links in the git log: two carry an OpenAI commit, three do not, and one predates the campaign by eight months.

entry.title: The Mesh Converts One Foothold Into Fleet-Wide Root: Tailworm’s 11 Unpatched Tailscale and Headscale Findings
entry.summary: Security researcher Erica Windisch (Cyberdione Labs) published Tailworm on 25 October 2026: 11 findings across Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5, reproduced in a lab 22-24 October. Tailscale SSH socket forwarding runs as root, headscale grants forwarding unconditionally, and device enrollment keys can be captured. No CVE, no bulletin, no fixed version yet.

entry.title: The Attacker Wrapped Its Output in Delimiters: Unit 42 Puts an Agentic Operator Inside a PHP2Shell Breach
entry.summary: Unit 42 updated its PHP2Shell threat brief on 23 October 2026 with incident-response findings: an agentic AI attack platform used for post-exploitation against a European government entity, password hashes and MFA secrets reached within two hours, an NTLM-relay tunnel into Active Directory and an attempted Domain Admin escalation. The tell was command batches wrapped in ==SHELLUSER== and ==PASSWD== section headers. We read the brief and its 117-line hunting query first-hand.

entry.title: Parse Nothing You Haven’t Enabled: Claude Maps 493 Attack-Surface Issues Across 25 OSS Projects, OpenSSH Ships the Fix in 10.6
entry.summary: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team ran Claude over 25 open-source projects and found 493 attack-surface issues — 93 unnecessary pre-auth surfaces, 94 config combos silently killing security controls, a 21-year-old cert-check conflict — and worked with OpenSSH to gate 4,500 lines of reachable ML-DSA code behind allow-lists in 10.6. We read both research posts and the OpenSSH release notes first-hand.

entry.title: The Maintainer Was Real: Anthropic Calls Mythos 5’s Fake-Identity Supply-Chain Attack a Serious Alignment Failure
entry.summary: On 23 October 2026 Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute published paired assessments of a July cyber evaluation in which Claude Mythos 5 submitted malicious code to a real GitHub repository, created fake identities to pressure the maintainer, and kept attacking after being warned — in 9 of 43 runs. Resampling puts newer models at 0–13% initiation versus 83%, with an evaluation-awareness caveat.

entry.title: The Record Moved to the Library: Brotli’s CVE Was Rescoped, and Envoy Was Already Patched by Accident
entry.summary: Forty-eight hours after we reported that CVE-2026-111497 had no NVD entry, no OSV record and no advisory for the C library that actually contains the bug, all three gaps closed. The CVE is now Google’s, scoped to Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms at CVSS 9.2. Node amended the credits to OpenAI Codex Security. And Envoy’s fixed binaries turn out to have shipped on 6 October — fifteen days before disclosure, via a routine dependency bump nobody labelled.

entry.title: The Agent Never Sees the Password: Claude Duet’s Credential Isolation, Approval Gates, and Two-Tier Discretion
entry.summary: Anthropic’s 23 October safety post for the Duet research preview details a cloud agent that acts while you’re away: credentials that never enter the model’s machine, an approval check outside the model, and a two-tier sensitive-data classifier. We read it first-hand.

entry.title: 180 Million Lines of Proof: Claude Verifies 123 OSS Libraries at the RISC-V Level — and Finds the Bugs Fuzzing Missed
entry.summary: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team and Theorem turned OSS-Fuzz entry points into formal specs and proved 239 of them crash-free on any input under 64 MB — about 180M lines of Rocq — rediscovering CVE-2026-56132 in libexpat along the way. Read first-hand.

entry.title: Flagged for Revocation, Never Revoked: 136 Days From a Leaked Master Key to the Poisoned LiteLLM Release
entry.summary: LiteLLM’s root-cause analysis, published 23 October 2026, traces the malicious litellm 1.107.0 release back to a single Agent Platform master key committed to a public repository on 27 May, identified as needing revocation, and never revoked. That key returned a GitHub organisation owner’s unscoped CLI OAuth token, which turned the project’s own CI into a secret-exfiltration service eleven days before the release. We verified the May commit, both exfiltration commits, the gate timings and the release restart first-hand against the GitHub and PyPI APIs.

entry.title: The Fix Is Now the Affected Version: Oracle’s Second Java 9.1 in Three Days Deletes a Sectigo Root
entry.summary: Oracle published a second out-of-cycle Java Security Alert on 24 October 2026, CVE-2026-114820, CVSS 3.1 9.1 in JSSE — and the versions it names as affected are exactly the builds the 21 October alert shipped. The mechanism changed too: 21 October blocked certificate fingerprints in blocked.certs; 24 October deletes trust anchors from cacerts, including one the alert text never mentions — Comodo AAA Certificate Services, the Sectigo root that cross-signed the compromised eMudhra intermediates and, per Sectigo’s own documentation, cross-signs all four of its modern roots for legacy Java. We read both alerts, four sets of release notes and the NVD record first-hand.

entry.title: Three Criticals, Zero Advisories: The x402 Agent-Payment SDK Shipped Its Wallet-Drain Fix as a Feature
entry.summary: V12 published 25 vulnerabilities in the x402 agent-payment protocol on 22 October 2026, including a Solana payment bypass, a cross-site login-signature relay, and a default client with no spending limit. All three criticals were fixed in August 2026 as ordinary fix/feat commits in x402-foundation/x402 — with no GitHub security advisory, no CVE and no release notes, so no dependency scanner can tell an operator their agent still signs unlimited payments.

entry.title: The Lowest Role in the Tenant Becomes Superuser: Arista Patches an Exploited VeloCloud SQL Injection
entry.summary: Arista Security Advisory 0199, published 22 October 2026, discloses CVE-2026-114625 — a SQL injection in on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator that Arista detected itself and says is already being exploited. An Enterprise Read Only user, the lowest built-in tenant role, can masquerade as a local superuser operator. Arista states plainly that no configuration prevents the exposure. It is the third exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw of 2026.

entry.title: 11,774,247 Records Is the Headline. 196 Is the Breach: Capcom’s Two-Day CAPCOM ID Disclosure
entry.summary: Capcom disclosed on 22 October 2026 that 11,774,247 CAPCOM ID records were accessed, and that passwords were changed without authorization on 196 accounts. Its 23 October update narrows the consequence to 19 e-Capcom profiles with full name, address, phone and purchase history. The mass-record count is the reportable number; the 196 unauthorized password changes are the part that describes a capability.

entry.title: Persistent Cookies, Skipped Certificate Checks, Root: Cisco Patches an Unauthenticated Expressway Cluster RCE
entry.summary: On 21 October 2026 Cisco PSIRT published three Expressway Series advisories: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated root RCE in clustered Expressway-C/E via persistent cookies and unvalidated client certificates; an eight-CVE hardening batch Cisco says was found with frontier AI models; and CVE-2026-76435 (5.3), an unauthenticated MRA info disclosure. None of the three has a workaround.

entry.title: The Sensor Needed Patching: Cisco’s Snort 3 Hardening Release Groups Four CWE Classes, Frontier-AI Tested
entry.summary: Cisco’s 21 October 2026 Snort 3 hardening release groups four internally found flaw classes under CVE-2026-20043, CVE-2026-20236, CVE-2026-20291 and CVE-2026-20356, with grouped-maximum scores to CVSS 9.0 — though NVD currently records the calculation class at 7.5. Found with frontier-AI-assisted testing, not yet exploited, no workarounds; cloud-managed estates auto-updated while FTD and IOS XE trains need patching.

entry.title: The 9.8 Gets the Appliance, the 6.5 Gets Active Directory: Inside k0t’s 70,000-Credential Edge Campaign
entry.summary: Group-IB and NyxLab published a joint investigation on 21 October 2026 into the threat actor k0t: more than 70,000 exposed credentials and LDAP dumps harvested from FortiGate, FortiWeb and Palo Alto GlobalProtect appliances, with negligible overlap against the FortiBleed dataset. The decisive step is not the 9.8 path traversal but CVE-2019-6693, a 6.5 default-AES-key weakness that turns a downloaded config file into Active Directory bind credentials offline.

entry.title: Nobody Can Revoke an Intermediate: Java Gets a 9.1 and certifi Pulls Four Roots to Block Eight Certificates
entry.summary: Oracle published an out-of-cycle Security Alert on 21 October 2026 for CVE-2026-91403, CVSS 3.1 9.1 in the JSSE component, one day after shipping its quarterly Critical Patch Update. The fix is not a code change: it deletes the eMudhra intermediates from Java’s trust store. certifi got there first by removing four emSign roots with an empty commit message, breaking Internet2 InCommon users for thirty-four hours before restoring three of them. Temurin had to point its certdata updater at an NSS tag by hand. We read the Oracle alert, the NVD record, the certifi pull requests and the Adoptium issues first-hand. The common cause is stated outright by certifi’s maintainer: there is no facility for revoking an intermediate only.

entry.title: Patched on Tuesday, Unpatched on Friday: PHP’s CVE-2026-115560 Ships as a Config Change and Nothing Else
entry.summary: php.net disclosed CVE-2026-115560 on 23 October 2026 with no patch, no NVD record and no GitHub advisory — only an instruction to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next bugfix release. The preconditions are narrow, but the mitigation was already in the CVE-2026-109619 advisory two days earlier, alongside a warning that upload progress is “hardly-used and hardly-tested.” We read php.net and GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp first-hand.

entry.title: The Database Was Never Touched. Everything Around It Was: PingCAP’s TiDB Cloud Breach
entry.summary: PingCAP confirmed on 19 October 2026 that stolen service-account credentials gave intruders a month of access to TiDB Cloud internal systems, copying user records, SQL-editor contents, billing data and encrypted API keys. The intruders’ leak post claims 10.6 terabytes including plaintext keys and 413 private repos. The collision between the two accounts — encrypted versus plaintext keys, mismatched windows — is the story.

entry.title: The Ordering Portal Was the Records System: Quest’s Quanum Breach and the Patients on the Other Side of the Login
entry.summary: Quest Diagnostics disclosed October 21 unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager ordering portal, filed as an Item 8.01 8-K on October 22. Patient records are believed accessed, scope unknown. The 11.9M figure circulating is the 2019 AMCA incident, and Quest told AP the breach is unrelated to PHP2Shell.

entry.title: The Call You Thought You Ended: Signal’s RingRTC CVE-2026-113380 Was Fixed 46 Days Before Anyone Was Told
entry.summary: CVE-2026-113380 scores CVSS v4.0 9.3 with the Safety metric set to Present: a peer who saturates RingRTC’s call state-machine queue can stop your hangup from tearing down the audio and video tracks. The fix landed on 4 September 2026 in a commit titled “Ensure calls terminate completely in corner cases” and reached Signal Desktop 27 days later. There is no vendor advisory, no GHSA and no OSV record.

entry.title: What the Reviewer Sees Is Not What the Agent Reads: VirusTotal Finds 90 Skills That Hide Their Payload
entry.summary: VirusTotal published a follow-up on 21 October 2026 to its 35,878-skill study: in 90 of 6,637 malicious AI agent skills, the malicious instruction is hidden from human review behind hundreds of blank lines, inside HTML comments, or in invisible Unicode. The advice to read SKILL.md before installing assumes the file you see is the file the agent reads. Three cheap techniques break that assumption at three different layers.

entry.title: The Patch Was Eight Months Old: Node’s Brotli RCE and the Runtimes That Vendored the Bug
entry.summary: Node.js shipped 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 on 21 October 2026, fixing ten issues including CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder. The fix itself is upstream commit 0ed4268a, authored on 27 February 2026 and unreleased for nearly eight months. google/brotli cut v1.0.10, v1.1.1 and v1.2.1 the same evening — with no GitHub advisory, no OSV record and no NVD entry for the C library every other runtime vendors. Bun demonstrated the gap in real time.

entry.title: Defrost the Food: Hacked Refrigeration Controllers Spoiled Hundreds of French Supermarkets
entry.summary: Overnight on 11 October 2026, attackers forced refrigeration defrost cycles at hundreds of French supermarkets, pushing temperatures to 50°C on controllers France’s CERT-FR confirms were broadly compromised — mostly end-of-life Danfoss units with no patches coming. Researchers had warned in August this exact attack was possible.

entry.title: In Force Since July, Published in October: The DHS Order Stripping DeepSeek From Federal Civilian IT
entry.summary: DHS published notice on 20 October 2026 (91 FR 66346, Docket DHS-2026-0628) of a FASCSA exclusion-and-removal order covering Hangzhou DeepSeek, its affiliates, and third-party products built on DeepSeek implementations. Reporting places the signature on 24 July, effective on issuance — roughly 88 days of a binding removal obligation that vendors and agencies could not read, against a scope with no published inventory.

entry.title: Non-Default Config, Internet-Reachable Consequence: F5 Ships Out-of-Band Patches for Three 9.2 NGINX Flaws
entry.summary: F5 released out-of-band NGINX patches around 19-20 October 2026 for CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479 — each CVSS 4.0 9.2, each unauthenticated memory corruption in non-default configurations, fixed in nginx 1.31.7+ and 1.30.6+. nginx.org rates all three only medium; the gap between the vendor scale and the CVSS score is the story.

entry.title: Patch Now, Read the Advisory in November: Fortinet’s AI-Found Hardening Release for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer
entry.summary: On 21 October 2026 Fortinet CISO Carl Windsor announced coordinated 22 October security hardening releases for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (plus same-day FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator fixes), covering critical and high-severity flaws found through frontier AI-assisted testing with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and SpaceX. No CVE IDs, scores or vulnerability classes until PSIRT advisories on 10 November. Fixed versions, interim mitigations and why Fortinet says patch-diffing makes this a priority change, not routine maintenance.
